title: Lisse coefficients on an open relative affine line over an integer model
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Work in the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For any separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$ consists of a quasi-compact open immersion $j$ and a proper morphism $p$ with $h=pj$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]; write $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $Y=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra $R$ (a commutative ring generated by finitely many elements as a ring). Assume that the additive order of every element of $\Lambda$ is invertible on $Y$. Let $U\subseteq\mathbf A^1_Y$ be an open subscheme [def-nagata-relative-affine-space], let $f:U\to Y$ be the restricted projection, and let $L$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $U_{\Et}$ locally isomorphic on an etale cover to constant sheaves of finite $\Lambda$-modules [def-constructible-locally-constant] [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Regard $L$ as a complex in degree zero. For every compactification $c$ of $f$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, $\mathcal H^q(Rf_!^cL)$ is constructible on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

source.place: Tag 0GKY, label lemma-loc-constant-shriek-rel-dim-1; specialization to finite rings and affine finite-type integer bases

proof.text: Finite type over the Noetherian ring of integers makes the base Noetherian. The restricted relative-line projection is smooth of relative dimension one, so its source is locally Noetherian; as an open of the affine Noetherian relative line it is Noetherian and quasi-compact. Choose a finite affine open cover, adjoining the empty open to avoid a nonempty-index assumption. Separatedness over the affine base implies that intersections of affine opens are affine. The restricted morphisms remain smooth of relative dimension one. It suffices to handle affine smooth relative curves, then glue this finite affine cover by relative Mayer--Vietoris.

source.place: Tag 0GKY; affine-cover expansion required to apply 0GKX

proof.text: The positive integer card(Lambda) annihilates Lambda and hence every sheaf of Lambda-modules. Induct on a positive annihilator n. The n=1 case is the zero sheaf. Otherwise choose a prime ell dividing n. The kernel--image short exact sequence for multiplication by ell has kernel killed by ell and image killed by n/ell<n. Both remain finite locally constant: kernels and cokernels of morphisms of finite locally constant sheaves over the finite, hence Noetherian, coefficient ring remain finite locally constant, and the image is isomorphic to a coimage. Applying the triangulated compactly supported derived image and the weak-Serre closure of constructible cohomology reduces the assertion to sheaves killed by one prime.

Apply the prime-to-torsion filtration cover input to the affine Noetherian $W$ and $F$. It gives $g:T\to W$, affine clopen components $T_a$, filtrations by constant finite modules on each $T_a$, and constant fibre cardinality $d$ prime to $\ell$. The module trace-degree calculation on algebraically closed stalks gives a $\Lambda$-linear $t:g_*g^{-1}F\to F$ with $t\eta=d\,\mathrm{id}_F$. Choose a natural number $a$ with $ad\equiv1\pmod{\ell}$; since $\ell F=0$, the map $at$ retracts $\eta$. Finite direct-image exactness for abelian sheaves implies exactness for these module sheaves too: the underlying direct image is the abelian direct image and a sequence of module sheaves is exact exactly when its underlying abelian sequence is exact. Using the module direct-image construction, take an injective resolution of a degree-zero module sheaf. Exactness makes its termwise direct image a resolution of its direct image, so the computation of derived direct image gives $Rg_*=g_*$ on degree-zero sheaves. Choose a compactification of $hg$ by Nagata: $T$ is finite over the affine $W$, hence affine and quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $hg$ is separated of finite type over the affine $Y$. A finite morphism is proper, so the identity compactification gives $Rg_!=Rg_*$. Shriek composition and compactification independence identify $Rh_!g_*g^{-1}F\cong R(hg)_!g^{-1}F$. Applying the additive $Rh_!$ to the split maps shows $Rh_!F$ is a retract of this latter object, hence each of its cohomology sheaves is a retract as well. The cover gives its degree condition on algebraically closed fields. This suffices: the trace is the counit of the reverse finite-etale adjunction, and the degree identity is checked on algebraic-closure stalks; the public theorem's stronger separably-closed-field hypothesis is not needed for that calculation.

For a chosen compactification $c=(j,p)$, exactness of module extension by zero and the exact-functor derived theorem make $j_!$ triangulated. Module direct image is additive left exact and its source has enough injectives, so the right-derived theorem makes $Rp_*$ triangulated. Thus $Rp_*j_!$ is additive and triangulated: apply the two functors successively to a distinguished triangle and compose their shift isomorphisms. This applies to every compactification used below.

proof.text: Put $k_a=hg|_{T_a}:T_a\to Y$. The cover input makes $T_a$ affine and $g|_{T_a}$ etale. Since $W$ and $Y$ are affine, $h$ is affine; an affine morphism has affine inverse images of all affine opens, and a morphism between affine schemes is affine (localize the corresponding ring map). Affine morphisms are separated and quasi-compact by affine permanence. Smooth-relative-dimension permanence gives $k_a$ smooth of relative dimension $0+1=1$. It is finite type: $h$ is finitely presented, and $g|_{T_a}$ is finite, as a clopen summand of the finite cover (on rings, it is an idempotent summand of a finite module). Nagata supplies a compactification of $k_a$. Apply the constant-coefficient relative-dimension-one theorem to every constant quotient $Q_{a,i}$ in the cover input; every $H^q(R(k_a)_!Q_{a,i})$ is constructible.

proof.text: Apply the existing finite-filtration cohomology devissage theorem to the compactly supported derived image and the weak Serre class of constructible sheaves. A generic private adapter converts the zero initial subobject into equality with bottom and transports the constant-quotient isomorphisms. The resulting induction starts with zero, uses short-exact-sequence triangles at successive steps, and identifies the terminal top subobject with the original sheaf. The adapter checks the categorical identifications over abstract categories before specializing to concrete sheaves.

proof.text: Write $i_a:T_a\hookrightarrow T$. Apply the disjoint-open-extension biproduct theorem to the finite disjoint open cover of $T$ and $G=g^{-1}F$: $G\cong\bigoplus_a i_{a!}(G|_{T_a})$. Each $i_a$ has compactification $(i_a,\mathrm{id}_T)$, so its candidate shriek is the exact $i_{a!}$. Additivity of $R(hg)_!$ preserves this finite biproduct, and shriek composition identifies its $a$-th image with $R(k_a)_!(G|_{T_a})$. Thus $R(hg)_!G\cong\bigoplus_a R(k_a)_!(G|_{T_a})$. Applying cohomology preserves the biproduct relations, so every cohomology sheaf is the finite sum of the constructible component cohomology sheaves. A finite sum of constructible sheaves is constructible by repeated extension closure applied to $0\to A\to A\oplus B\to B\to0$.

proof.text: The trace unit and its scalar multiple give a retract of the original sheaf from the finite pushforward of its pullback. Map this retract through the degree-zero functor, the compactly supported derived image, and each cohomology functor. Constructible sheaves are closed under retracts, giving the prime-torsion case on an affine smooth relative curve. Apply the kernel--image induction of step 2 to obtain the result for every finite locally constant sheaf. An arbitrary affine source is transported to the spectrum of its global sections by its canonical isomorphism; shriek composition and the extension-by-zero adjunction identify the corresponding compactifications.

proof.text: Induct on the size of a nonempty finite affine open cover of U. The one-open case is the affine case already proved. At the induction step write U=V1 union V2, where V2 is the last affine open and V1 is the union of the other opens. The intersection V1 cap V2 has an affine cover of the same size as V1, obtained by intersecting its cover with V2; these intersections are affine since U is separated over the affine base. Apply the induction hypothesis to V1 and to V1 cap V2 and the affine case to V2. Restrictions of the finite locally constant sheaf stay finite locally constant. All opens are quasi-compact in the Noetherian source, so Nagata supplies compactifications. The natural extension-by-zero short exact sequence for the two-open cover gives a distinguished triangle after the degree-zero inclusion and compactly supported derived image. Shriek composition identifies the three extended restrictions with the chosen compactly supported images of the opens and their intersection. This is the relative Mayer--Vietoris argument at the sheaf level. The class of complexes with constructible cohomology is triangulated and closed under finite biproducts, so the third vertex has constructible cohomology. The initial affine cover was enlarged by the empty open, so this argument includes the empty-source case.
